# SiteShaper

> SiteShaper turns a lot and a program into a schematic scheme book: site plan with setbacks, auto-generated floor plates, MEP location markers for single-family, and the numbers table — ready for your architect to review and build from.

SiteShaper is a free web tool at https://siteshaper.nesohq.com/. It runs in the browser with no account.
It is for owners, small developers and builders testing what fits on a lot before hiring an architect.

## Questions SiteShaper answers

- **How many units or how much building actually fits on my lot?** Buildable area is the lot minus front, side and rear setbacks, then limited by lot coverage, height, parking and any easements.
- **What is a schematic site plan?** A scaled drawing showing the lot, its setbacks, the building footprint, access and parking — enough to test whether a program fits and to start a conversation with a planner.
- **How do setbacks change what I can build?** They shrink the buildable rectangle from every side that has one, and on a narrow lot the side setbacks usually decide the answer before density does.
- **Can I get floor plans without hiring an architect first?** You can get schematic plates that show room sizes, adjacencies and proportions — useful for testing a program and pricing a scope.

## Use it

- [Open SiteShaper](https://siteshaper.nesohq.com/)
